_readme: Specialty coffee, researched Oct 2026 (Sonnet agent + spot checks). Coordinates estimated from addresses.

items.name: Espresso Embassy
items.hours: Mon–Fri 07:30–17:00 · Sat–Sun 08:30–17:00 (sources disagree on closing: some say 19:00 on weekdays)
items.blurb: Budapest's flagship specialty roaster-bar, ranked 17th in a June 2026 list of Europe's best coffee shops. Small, busy and serious about the brew. About 15 minutes' walk from the Airbnb.
items.tip: Get a cortado or a filter, plus a pastry. Go early on Saturday or you'll queue. Flat white about 1,500 HUF (£3.50).

items.name: Madal Café (Király utca)
items.hours: Mon–Fri 07:30–19:30 · Sat–Sun 08:30–19:30 (third-party listings, not checked with the cafe)
items.blurb: Big, bright branch of a proper Budapest specialty chain, opened late 2024 on the street you're staying on. Good beans, decent croissants and room for the lads to sit.
items.tip: Single-origin filter or a flat white, plus a croissant. Easy first stop of the day on the walk into town.

items.name: Kern Collective Coffee
items.hours: Check Google Maps for opening times on the day
items.blurb: Student-friendly specialty bar five minutes from the Airbnb, opened 2022. Scruffy in a good way, with free wifi and takeaway if you're in a rush for the next pub.
items.tip: One of the two closest proper coffees to the Airbnb. Grab a flat white to go on the way to anywhere (about 1,200 HUF, £3).

items.name: % Arabica Király
items.hours: Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00 · Sat–Sun 09:00–18:00 (listings conflict on weekend closing)
items.blurb: Minimalist Japanese coffee bar with Zsolnay tiles and its own roaster, opened early 2025, a three-minute stagger from the Airbnb. Pricier than the locals' places, but the coffee is smooth.
items.tip: Go for the latte or the Kyoto-style coffee with condensed milk. Expect to pay a bit over 1,500 HUF (£3.50+).

items.name: Fekete
items.hours: Mon–Fri 08:00–19:00 · Sat 08:30–19:00 · Sun 09:00–18:00 (another guide says daily 08:00–19:00)
items.blurb: Tucked in a courtyard near Astoria. A tiny espresso bar plus a separate brew and food room, so you can actually sit. A reliable specialty pick that's still on the 2026 lists.
items.tip: Try a V60 or AeroPress, and the homemade cake. Weekend mornings get packed and the bar is tiny.

items.name: My Little Melbourne
items.hours: Mon–Fri 07:30–17:00 · Sat–Sun 08:30–17:00 (an older review says weekdays to 19:00)
items.blurb: One of Budapest's original specialty coffee shops (since 2012), Aussie style and still on the 2026 third-wave lists. Small, friendly and a short walk from Király utca.
items.tip: Flat white and a toastie or something eggy for breakfast. Good hangover fixer, about 1,400 HUF (£3.30) for the coffee.

items.name: Dorado Café
items.hours: Mon–Fri 08:30–17:00 · Sat 09:00–17:00 · Sun 09:00–15:00 (directory listing, not checked with the cafe)
items.blurb: Calm, small specialty cafe near Klauzál tér, run by a Hungarian-Spanish couple. Quiet during the week, so a good place to recover before the evening starts.
items.tip: Espresso tonic or avocado toast. Short menu, friendly baristas, a ten minute walk from the Airbnb.

items.name: Vivina's Café & Roastery
items.blurb: Roastery and cafe with a proper terrace, ranked 79th in a 2026 list of Europe's best coffee shops. Strong brunch menu, so it does the job for a long, slow Saturday morning.
items.tip: Beans are roasted in house: get a filter, then a breakfast plate. Sunday opens late (09:30), so no early starts.

items.name: Mantra Specialty Coffee Bar
items.hours: Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 · Sat–Sun 08:30–18:00 (other listings give Sunday closed or later times)
items.blurb: Compact specialty bar near Ferenciek tere that rotates two guest roasters a day. A nerdy, quiet stop if you're wandering the Váci utca end of town.
items.tip: Ask what the two roasters are today and go filter. Check Sunday opening before you make a trip of it.

items.name: Kontakt
items.hours: Mon–Fri 08:00–16:00 or 18:00 · Sat 09:00–16:00 or 17:00 · Sun closed or 09:00–17:00 (listings conflict: check before you go)
items.blurb: A purists' spot on the Kiskörút, a short stroll from Deák tér. Rotating European and Hungarian roasters on espresso and filter, and no fuss.
items.tip: Plain coffee only, no sugar bowl in sight. Check Sunday opening first.

items.name: Tamp & Pull
items.hours: Mon–Fri 07:30–18:00 · Sat 08:00–17:00 · Sun 08:00–15:00 (another listing says Sun closed)
items.blurb: Respected small espresso bar south of the centre, on the 2026 third-wave lists. Worth the walk or a tram if you're heading towards the river or Fővám tér anyway.
items.tip: Espresso or a flat white, standing at the bar. Ask about the Sopron roast. Not near Király utca, so combine it with other plans.
